what_happened: On 2026-11-03 the person running Athena raised the fix for config-key landings to urgent priority. The focus-and-caps job (20261101-085726-z7dg) landed a new setting. The running installed copy did not know the new key, so the batch stopped with the job marked 'failed twice'. This was the second time, after the same failure on 1 Nov. The person running Athena reinstalled the build by hand and set the focus to speed, as the owner directed. The fix had been queued but had not run. No acceptance criteria, findings or checks are listed for the event.
cause: Athena's landing runs on the already installed build. Nothing compares a job's new config keys with what that build accepts, and nothing rebuilds or restarts the running copy after a landing that changes the config schema. The fix for this was queued at ordinary priority, with nothing connecting a repeat batch stop to its rank. Athena does not count repeat failures per class, so only a person noticing the repeat raises the priority. The drain also treats the resulting error as a plain job failure ('failed twice') rather than as a stale build.
prevention: Two code changes together. First, before dispatching or landing a job that adds a config field, check that the running build accepts the key. If not, land the job on a path that rebuilds the installed build first, or hold the job with a clear 'installed build is stale' message instead of counting it as failed. Second, after any landing that changes Athena's own code or config schema, have drain rebuild and re-exec itself, or stop cleanly. This removes the whole class of config key unknown to the installed build, including the manual reinstall. Also count repeat failures in the same class so the fix's priority rises on its own.
proposed_request: Make landings that add a new athena.toml key safe for a running drain. (1) When a job's diff adds a config key or section, the drain must check, before landing, that the installed build accepts it. If it does not, the drain must rebuild or reinstall Athena from the landed code and continue, or else pause the line with the message 'installed build is older than landed config', never marking the job failed. (2) After any landing that changes Athena's own code or config schema, the drain must restart on the new build before reading the next item. (3) A job held for a stale build must not count toward 'failed twice'. Acceptance: a test lands a job that adds a new config key with an older build running, and shows the drain finishes the landing, the job ends landed, and the next queued item runs on the new build. A second test shows a stale build is reported as such and not as a job failure. Do not change the focus setting or other config values.
